Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

37167	    ``site_policy``, the expected ``decision_site_policy``, the current
37168	    ``keyring`` and the verification ``moment`` are consulted -- no file

37170	    validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes all
37171	    four policy digests, and re-tallies the bound per-decision rows
37172	    purely from the signed payload: the original-order input digest
37173	    bindings, the issuer/id row ordering, same-site duplicate and
37174	    contradiction markings, cross-site complete declaration agreement
37175	    (the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions, the
37176	    term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status together),
37177	    the threshold outcome and the claimed common declaration, together
37178	    with a full re-tally of every counted declaration against the
37179	    signer site policy threshold.  It then checks the HMAC-SHA256
37180	    against the key the *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact
37181	    issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later
37182	    revocation or expiry rejects the aggregate with no fallback.

37188	    ``authorizationPolicyDigest``, ``sitePolicyDigest``,
37189	    ``decisionSitePolicyDigest``, ``declaration``, ``status`` and
37190	    ``version`` (the integer 1) -- repeated calls return equal but
37191	    mutually independent objects sharing no mutable structure, and
37192	    unauthenticated identities or boundaries never enter a result.  A
37193	    non-bytes aggregate or a field of the wrong type raises
37194	    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); a null
37195	    value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy,

37198	    binding raises
37199	    :class:`InvalidAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError` (a

33854	def _cda_assert_extends(
33855	    previous: dict, full_inputs: list[str], increment: list[dict],
33856	    unchanged: bool,
33857	) -> None:
33858	    """Enforce the append-only decision prefix and disjoint identities.
33859	
33860	    The predecessor's decision digests must remain the ordered prefix of
33861	    the stage -- nothing is deleted, changed or reordered -- and a
33862	    non-empty increment adds only new packet digests and new item ids.
33863	    An unchanged policy must add at least one decision; a rotation may
33864	    re-seal the identical sequence with an empty increment.
33865	    """
33866	    prefix_inputs = previous[_CFADA_INPUTS]
33867	    if unchanged and not increment:
33868	        raise _cda_chain_invalid("an unchanged policy requires new decisions")
33869	    if len(full_inputs) < len(prefix_inputs):
33870	        raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33871	            "the decision sequence must extend the predecessor"
33872	        )
33873	    if full_inputs[:len(prefix_inputs)] != prefix_inputs:
33874	        raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33875	            "the decision sequence must keep the predecessor as an ordered "
33876	            "prefix; history must not be deleted, changed or reordered"
33877	        )
33878	    prefix_digests = set(prefix_inputs)
33879	    prefix_ids = {row[ID] for row in previous[PA_ITEMS]}
33880	    seen_digests: set[str] = set()
33881	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
33882	    for item in increment:
33883	        digest = hashlib.sha256(item[CDA_PACKET]).hexdigest()
33884	        if digest in prefix_digests or digest in seen_digests:
33885	            raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33886	                "a decision packet already in the prefix must not be appended "
33887	                "again"
33888	            )
33889	        seen_digests.add(digest)
33890	        item_id = item[ID]
33891	        if item_id in prefix_ids or item_id in seen_ids:
33892	            raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33893	                f"decision item id {item_id!r} is already part of the chain"
33894	            )
33895	        seen_ids.add(item_id)

33898	def _cda_assert_transition(previous: dict, verdict: dict) -> None:
33899	    """Enforce the per-hop verdict state machine for a decision aggregate.
33900

33902	    ``accepted`` or ``conflicted``; an ``accepted`` head only keeps the
33903	    identical common declaration or advances to ``conflicted`` (it
33904	    never falls back to insufficient or swaps declarations); a
33905	    ``conflicted`` verdict can never be masked by a later majority.

33911	            raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33912	                "a conflicted aggregate can never be outvoted or fall back"
33913	            )

33915	        if new_status == PA_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT:
33916	            raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33917	                "an accepted aggregate must not fall back to insufficient"
33918	            )
33919	        if new_status == PA_STATUS_ACCEPTED:
33920	            if verdict[_CFADA_DECLARATION] != previous[_CFADA_DECLARATION]:
33921	                raise _cda_chain_invalid(
33922	                    "an accepted aggregate may only keep the same common "
33923	                    "declaration"
33924	                )

34131	        )

34143	        raise TypeError("successor signature must be a str")

34280	def supersede_decision_aggregate(
34281	    predecessor, increment, prune_policy, authorization_policy, old_policy,
34282	    new_policy, keyring, moment, effective_at, issuer, version
34283	):
34284	    """Issue one signed supersession successor over a decision aggregate.
34285	
34286	    ``predecessor`` is either the chain root (an
34287	    :func:`aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions` packet) or the
34288	    previous successor packet.  ``increment`` is the stage's decision
34289	    list in the exact shape of that aggregate's items -- each exactly a
34290	    unique non-empty ``id`` and ``decision`` bytes (an
34291	    :func:`adjudicate_chain_fork_aggregate_proofs` packet) -- and may be
34292	    empty only for a policy rotation.  The stage keeps every predecessor
34293	    decision verbatim as an ordered digest prefix and only appends the
34294	    increment; the original prune policy, the site authorization policy,
34295	    the root and existing statements are never deleted, changed or
34296	    reordered.  ``prune_policy`` is the invariant original
34297	    ``{"batch", "sites", "threshold"}`` pruning policy and
34298	    ``authorization_policy`` the invariant site authorization policy,
34299	    both fixed along the whole chain; only the **decision** site policy
34300	    may rotate: ``old_policy``/``new_policy`` carry exactly ``sites``,
34301	    ``threshold`` and a positive ``policyVersion`` -- unchanged sites and
34302	    threshold keep the version and require a non-empty increment, any
34303	    content change increments the version by exactly one, and the first
34304	    versioned policy over a root carries version 1 and must equal the
34305	    root's decision site policy.  ``effective_at`` is the hop's
34306	    non-negative effective moment and never moves backwards; ``moment``
34307	    is the issuance moment and ``issuer``/``version`` name the successor
34308	    sealing key, which must be authorized under both decision policies
34309	    and usable at both moments.
34310	
34311	    The successor verdict is recomputed in full from the full history:
34312	    supplemental decisions may move ``insufficient`` to ``accepted`` or
34313	    ``conflicted``; an ``accepted`` head only keeps the identical common
34314	    declaration or advances to ``conflicted``; and a ``conflicted``
34315	    verdict can never be masked by a later majority.
34316	
34317	    Returns canonical compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly ``payload`` and
34318	    ``signature``; the payload binds the root digest, predecessor
34319	    digest, height, the complete recomputed conclusion, the invariant
34320	    prune and site authorization policy digests, the old/new decision
34321	    policy digests, the policy version, the effective moment, the raw
34322	    decision increment (bytes as lowercase hex), the issuer and key
34323	    version and ``version`` (the integer 1), signed with HMAC-SHA256
34324	    under the exact issuer/version key.  A parameter or public field
34325	    type fault raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses
34326	    as an int); an empty value, duplicate increment id, illegal version,
34327	    wrong policy count or backwards moment raises :class:`ValueError`; a
34328	    malformed root raises
34329	    :class:`InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`; a malformed

34878	def verify_decision_aggregate_chains(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy,
34879	                                     keyring, moment):
34880	    """Verify a batch of decision aggregate chains and spot successor forks.
34881	
34882	    Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty ``id``, its ``root``
34883	    aggregate packet, its ordered ``successors`` packets and its
34884	    per-stage ``policies`` history; ``prune_policy`` is the invariant
34885	    original pruning policy and ``authorization_policy`` the invariant
34886	    site authorization policy shared by every chain, and ``keyring`` and
34887	    ``moment`` keep their single-chain meaning.  The whole batch
34888	    structure -- every key set, element type, policy count and the
34889	    shared materials -- is validated before any chain is verified, so
34890	    only batch-level faults raise (container, element or field type
34891	    faults :class:`TypeError`, a :class:`bool` never posing as an int;
34892	    an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set, a wrong
34893	    policy count or an illegal moment :class:`ValueError`).
34894	
34895	    Each chain is then verified independently, in strict input order,
34896	    through the exact :func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chain` rules: one
34897	    chain's failure never stops a later chain or changes an earlier
34898	    report.  A root fault reports ``invalid-root``, a successor or
34899	    chain-binding fault ``invalid-chain`` and a credential or signature
34900	    fault ``unauthenticated``, each with a null ``result``; a passing
34901	    chain reports ``verified``.
34902	
34903	    The verified chains are grouped by their ``rootDigest`` and only
34904	    successor trajectories under the same root are compared: the same
34905	    predecessor digest pointing at two distinct successor digests is a
34906	    fork, while a plain prefix extension (one chain growing longer along
34907	    the same packets) is not.  Every verified chain crossing a forking
34908	    edge is reclassified ``conflicted`` with its verified result kept
34909	    and its ``error`` fixed to ``"forked-decision-aggregate-chain"``;
34910	    invalid and unauthenticated chains are never reclassified.
34911	
34912	    Returns a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``forks``, ``items`` and
34913	    ``version`` (the integer 1).  ``forks`` is sorted stably by
34914	    ``rootDigest`` then ``predecessorDigest``; each entry carries exactly
34915	    ``rootDigest``, ``predecessorDigest``, ``successors`` (the forking
34916	    successor digests, ascending) and ``ids`` (the ascending ids of the
34917	    chains crossing the edge).  Each item report preserves the input
34918	    order and carries, in this key order, ``error``, ``id``, ``result``
34919	    and ``status``.  No file is read or written and no input is
34920	    modified.
34921	    """
34922	    validated_items = _validated_fac_chain_batch(items)
34923	    _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
34924	    _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(authorization_policy)
34925	    _validated_keyring(keyring)
34926	    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
34927	
34928	    reports: list[dict] = []
34929	    results: list[dict | None] = []
34930	    for item in validated_items:
34931	        report = _verify_cda_chain_item(
34932	            item, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, verify_moment
34933	        )
34934	        reports.append(report)
34935	        results.append(report[VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT])
34936	
34937	    # Fork detection within one root group: one predecessor digest
34938	    # pointing at two distinct successor digests, ignoring chains that
34939	    # did not verify.
34940	    groups: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
34941	    for item, result in zip(validated_items, results):
34942	        if result is None:
34943	            continue
34944	        nodes = _pac_chain_edge_nodes(item)
34945	        edges = groups.setdefault(nodes[0], {})
34946	        for upstream, downstream in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
34947	            edges.setdefault(upstream, set()).add(downstream)
34948	    fork_edges: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
34949	    for root_digest, edges in groups.items():
34950	        for upstream, digests in edges.items():
34951	            if len(digests) > 1:
34952	                fork_edges[(root_digest, upstream)] = sorted(digests)
34953	    edge_ids: dict[tuple[str, str], set[str]] = {
34954	        edge: set() for edge in fork_edges
34955	    }
34956	    if fork_edges:
34957	        for item, report, result in zip(validated_items, reports, results):
34958	            if result is None:
34959	                continue
34960	            nodes = _pac_chain_edge_nodes(item)
34961	            crosses_fork = False
34962	            for upstream in nodes[:-1]:
34963	                edge = (nodes[0], upstream)
34964	                if edge in fork_edges:
34965	                    edge_ids[edge].add(item[ID])
34966	                    crosses_fork = True
34967	            if crosses_fork:
34968	                report[STATUS] = PAC_CHAINS_CONFLICTED
34969	                report[CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR] = _CDA_CHAIN_ITEM_ERROR
34970	
34971	    forks = [
34972	        {
34973	            PAC_ROOT_DIGEST: root_digest,
34974	            PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST: predecessor,
34975	            PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: fork_edges[(root_digest, predecessor)],
34976	            _FORK_IDS: sorted(edge_ids[(root_digest, predecessor)]),
34977	        }
34978	        for root_digest, predecessor in sorted(fork_edges)
34979	    ]
34980	    return {
34981	        CHAINS_FORKS: forks,
34982	        ITEMS: reports,
34983	        VERSION: DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAINS_VERSION,
34984	    }

34998	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")

35000	        raise _cda_anchor_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc

35047	    anchor_moment = payload[CP_MOMENT]

35050	    if anchor_moment < 0:
35051	        raise _cda_anchor_invalid("payload moment must be non-negative")
35052	    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]

35054	        raise TypeError("payload issuer must be a str")
35055	    if issuer == "":
35056	        raise _cda_anchor_invalid("payload issuer must be a non-empty str")
35057	    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
35058	    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
35059	        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
35060	    if key_version <= 0:
35061	        raise _cda_anchor_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")

35082	    :func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chains` rules.  An anchor is sealed
35083	    only for the ``target`` chain when it is ``verified`` -- never
35084	    conflicted by a fork in this batch, invalid or unauthenticated --
35085	    and its head is ``accepted``; otherwise sealing raises
35086	    :class:`ValueError`.  Other chains' failures never stop the target's
35087	    anchor, though a fork it shares still reclassifies it.  The anchor
35088	    binds that chain's root digest, head digest and height together with
35089	    the head decision policy digest, the head policy version and the
35090	    sealing moment, and is signed with HMAC-SHA256 under the exact
35091	    ``issuer``/``version`` key usable at ``moment``.

35094	    ``signature``.  A parameter or public field type fault raises
35095	    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an
35096	    empty value, an unknown or duplicate target id, an illegal version
35097	    or a wrong policy count raises :class:`ValueError`; a chain fault
35098	    raises the underlying :class:`InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`
35099	    or :class:`InvalidAggregateChainError`; a signing credential fault
35100	    raises :class:`AuthenticationError`.  No file is read or written and
35101	    no input is modified.
35102	    """
35103	    validated_items = _validated_fac_chain_batch(items)
35104	    if not isinstance(target, str):
35105	        raise TypeError("target must be a str")
35106	    if target == "":
35107	        raise ValueError("target must be non-empty")
35108	    target_index = None
35109	    for position, item in enumerate(validated_items):
35110	        if item[ID] == target:
35111	            target_index = position
35112	            break
35113	    if target_index is None:
35114	        raise ValueError(f"unknown target id {target!r}")
35115	    _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
35116	    _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(authorization_policy)
35117	    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
35118	    seal_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
35119	    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
35120	        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
35121	    if issuer == "":
35122	        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
35123	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
35124	        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
35125	    if version <= 0:
35126	        raise ValueError("version must be positive")
35127	
35128	    report = verify_decision_aggregate_chains(
35129	        items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, seal_moment
35130	    )
35131	    target_report = report[ITEMS][target_index]
35132	    target_status = target_report[STATUS]
35133	    if target_status == PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_ROOT:
35134	        raise InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError(
35135	            target_report[CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR]
35136	        )
35137	    if target_status == PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_CHAIN:
35138	        # The report message already carries the chain-error prefix.
35139	        raise InvalidAggregateChainError(
35140	            target_report[CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR]
35141	        )
35142	    if target_status == PAC_CHAINS_UNAUTHENTICATED:
35143	        raise AuthenticationError(target_report[CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR])
35144	    if target_status != PAC_CHAINS_VERIFIED:
35145	        raise ValueError(
35146	            "an anchor seals only a verified target with no fork"
35147	        )
35148	    result = target_report[VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT]
35149	    if result[STATUS] != PA_STATUS_ACCEPTED:
35150	        raise ValueError("an anchor seals only an accepted head")
35151	    target_item = validated_items[target_index]
35152	    head_packet = (
35153	        target_item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS][-1]
35154	        if target_item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS] else target_item[PAC_BATCH_ROOT]
35155	    )
35156	    head_policy = _validated_pac_site_policy(
35157	        target_item[PAC_BATCH_POLICIES][-1]
35158	    )
35159	    if result[FAC_HEAD_DIGEST] != hashlib.sha256(head_packet).hexdigest():

35162	        validated_keyring, issuer, version, seal_moment

35165	        CDA_ROOT_DIGEST: result[CDA_ROOT_DIGEST],
35166	        FAC_HEAD_DIGEST: result[FAC_HEAD_DIGEST],
35167	        CDA_HEIGHT: result[CDA_HEIGHT],

35297	# -- Signed fork proofs over decision aggregate chain batches -----------------
35298	#
35299	# These entry points sit one layer above
35300	# ``sign_chain_fork_aggregate_proof``: that proof packages the
35301	# ``verify_chain_fork_aggregate_chains`` batch, while this layer packages
35302	# the ``verify_decision_aggregate_chains`` batch (decision aggregate
35303	# supersession chains).  It reuses the same proof envelope but binds the
35304	# two *invariant* policies that share the whole batch -- the original
35305	# prune policy and the site authorization policy; the versioned decision
35306	# site policy history is carried per stage inside the chain materials.
35307	# Adjudication additionally takes the site policy that authorizes the

"""Tests for supersession chains over cross-site chain fork aggregate
decision aggregates.

Covers :func:`supersede_decision_aggregate`,
:func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chain`,
:func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chains`,
:func:`seal_decision_aggregate_head` and
:func:`verify_decision_aggregate_head`: the canonical signed successor
packet and every binding (root, predecessor, height, the full
recomputed conclusion, the raw decision increment as hex, the invariant
prune and site authorization policy digests, the old/new decision policy
digests, policy version and effective moment), the per-hop verdict state
machine (insufficient to accepted/conflicted, accepted only kept or
upgraded, conflicted never masked), the append-only decision prefix with
unchanged-policy growth and rotation-only re-sealing, versioned decision
site policy rotation with a single policyVersion step, dual-policy
sealer authorization and credential usability at both the effective and
verification moments, offline hop-by-hop verification, bare-root
verification, the fresh chain summary with the common declaration
digest, batch verification with cross-chain successor fork detection and
the conflicted reclassification, the stable head anchor seal/reverify
rules, the distinct InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError /
InvalidAggregateChainError / InvalidAggregateAnchorError hierarchy, and
every error classification (including a bool never posing as an int),
input immutability and the purely offline guarantee.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import sys
import unittest
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from offline_coordination.replication import (
    AuthenticationError,
    InvalidAggregateAnchorError,
    InvalidAggregateChainError,
    InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError,
    aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions,
    seal_decision_aggregate_head,
    supersede_decision_aggregate,
    verify_decision_aggregate_chain,
    verify_decision_aggregate_chains,
    verify_decision_aggregate_head,
)

from test_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregates import (
    ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures,
)
from test_aggregate_prune_fork_decisions import decision_item
from test_fork_convergence import SECRET_COORD, compact, entry, parse
from test_prune_attestations import JUDGE, SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C
from test_supersede_chain_fork_aggregate import chain_item, plain, vpol

JUDGE_B = SITE_C

PACKET_KEYS = ["payload", "signature"]
SUCCESSOR_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "authorizationPolicyDigest", "decisions", "declaration",
    "effectiveAt", "height", "inputs", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "newPolicyDigest", "oldPolicyDigest", "policyVersion",
    "predecessorDigest", "prunePolicyDigest", "rootDigest", "status",
    "version",
]
INCREMENT_KEYS = ["decision", "id"]
CHAIN_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "rootDigest", "headDigest", "height", "policyVersion", "status",
    "commonDigest",
]
REPORT_KEYS = ["error", "id", "result", "status"]
BATCH_REPORT_KEYS = ["forks", "items", "version"]
FORK_KEYS = ["rootDigest", "predecessorDigest", "successors", "ids"]
ANCHOR_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "headDigest", "height", "issuer", "keyVersion", "moment",
    "policyDigest", "policyVersion", "rootDigest", "version",
]
ANCHOR_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "rootDigest", "headDigest", "height", "policyDigest", "policyVersion",
    "anchorDigest",
]

FORKED_ERROR = "forked-decision-aggregate-chain"


def rewrap(payload, secret=SECRET_COORD):
    """Re-sign an envelope payload into canonical compact packet bytes."""
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret), compact(payload), hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    return compact({"payload": payload, "signature": signature})


class DecisionAggregateChainFixtures(
    ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures, unittest.TestCase
):
    """Shared chain-layer roots, decisions, policies and chain builders."""

    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.auth = self.cauth()
        self.pv1 = vpol()
        self.pv2_t1 = vpol(2, threshold=1)
        self.pv1_3 = vpol(1, sites=(JUDGE, JUDGE_B, SITE_A), threshold=2)

        # A disagreeing decision carrying a distinct complete declaration.
        self.decision_other = self.make_cfa_decision(
            self.other_proofs(), issuer=SITE_A)

        # Chain-layer roots: one site (insufficient), two agreeing
        # (accepted) and two disagreeing declarations (conflicted).
        self.root_one = aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            [decision_item("one", self.decision_a)],
            self.policy, self.auth, self.dsp, self.ring, self.m, JUDGE, 1,
        )
        self.root_two = aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            self.cfa_decision_items(),
            self.policy, self.auth, self.dsp, self.ring, self.m, JUDGE, 1,
        )
        self.root_conf = aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            [decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
             decision_item("b", self.make_cfa_decision(
                 self.other_proofs(), issuer=JUDGE_B))],
            self.policy, self.auth, plain(self.pv1_3), self.ring, self.m,
            JUDGE, 1,
        )

    def dsucc(self, predecessor, increment, old=None, new=None,
              moment=None, effective=None, issuer=JUDGE, version=1,
              auth=None):
        return supersede_decision_aggregate(
            predecessor, increment,
            self.policy, self.auth if auth is None else auth,
            self.pv1 if old is None else old,
            self.pv1 if new is None else new,
            self.ring,
            self.m + 10 if moment is None else moment,
            self.m if effective is None else effective,
            issuer, version,
        )

    def dvchain(self, root, successors, policies=None, moment=None,
                auth=None):
        if policies is None:
            policies = [self.pv1] * (len(successors) + 1)
        if moment is None:
            moment = self.m + 10 * max(1, len(successors))
        return verify_decision_aggregate_chain(
            root, successors, self.policy,
            self.auth if auth is None else auth,
            policies, self.ring, moment,
        )

    def dcitem(self, item_id, root, successors, policies=None):
        if policies is None:
            policies = [self.pv1] * (len(successors) + 1)
        return chain_item(item_id, root, successors, policies)

    def dvchains(self, items, moment=None, auth=None, ring=None):
        return verify_decision_aggregate_chains(
            items, self.policy,
            self.auth if auth is None else auth,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m + 20 if moment is None else moment,
        )


class SuccessorShapeTest(DecisionAggregateChainFixtures):
    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_one, [decision_item("two", self.decision_b)])

    def test_canonical_compact_without_trailing_byte(self):
        self.assertIsInstance(self.raw, bytes)
        self.assertTrue(self.raw.endswith(b"}"))
        self.assertNotIn(b"\n", self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(compact(parse(self.raw)), self.raw)

    def test_top_and_payload_key_sets(self):
        data = parse(self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(data.keys()), PACKET_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(list(data["payload"].keys()),
                         SUCCESSOR_PAYLOAD_KEYS)

    def test_increment_is_bound_as_hex(self):
        decisions = parse(self.raw)["payload"]["decisions"]
        self.assertEqual(len(decisions), 1)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(decisions[0].keys()), INCREMENT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(decisions[0]["id"], "two")
        self.assertEqual(
            bytes.fromhex(decisions[0]["decision"]), self.decision_b)

    def test_height_root_and_policy_bindings(self):
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(payload["height"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["rootDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.root_one).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(payload["predecessorDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.root_one).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(payload["policyVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["effectiveAt"], self.m)
        self.assertEqual(payload["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["issuer"], JUDGE)
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["prunePolicyDigest"],
            parse(self.root_one)["payload"]["prunePolicyDigest"])
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["authorizationPolicyDigest"],
            parse(self.root_one)["payload"]["authorizationPolicyDigest"])


class BareRootVerifyTest(DecisionAggregateChainFixtures):
    def test_bare_root_verified_in_full(self):
        result = self.dvchain(self.root_two, [])
        self.assertEqual(list(result.keys()), CHAIN_RESULT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(result["rootDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.root_two).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(result["headDigest"], result["rootDigest"])
        self.assertEqual(result["height"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["policyVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
        self.assertIsNotNone(result["commonDigest"])

    def test_conflicted_bare_root_common_digest_is_null(self):
        result = self.dvchain(self.root_conf, [], policies=[self.pv1_3])
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "conflicted")
        self.assertIsNone(result["commonDigest"])

    def test_result_is_depth_independent_and_fresh(self):
        first = self.dvchain(self.root_two, [])
        second = self.dvchain(self.root_two, [])
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)


class GrowthAndStateMachineTest(DecisionAggregateChainFixtures):
    def test_insufficient_grows_to_accepted(self):
        raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_one, [decision_item("two", self.decision_b)])
        result = self.dvchain(self.root_one, [raw])
        self.assertEqual(result["height"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
        self.assertIsNotNone(result["commonDigest"])

    def test_insufficient_stays_insufficient_below_threshold(self):
        # A decision that does not authenticate adds no valid distinct
        # site, so the tally stays insufficient but keeps the declaration.
        raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_one, [decision_item("two", b"{}")])
        result = self.dvchain(self.root_one, [raw])
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "insufficient")
        self.assertIsNotNone(result["commonDigest"])

    def test_conflicted_can_never_be_masked(self):
        raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_conf,
            [decision_item("s", self.decision_b)],
            old=self.pv1_3, new=self.pv1_3,
        )
        self.assertEqual(parse(raw)["payload"]["status"], "conflicted")
        result = self.dvchain(
            self.root_conf, [raw], policies=[self.pv1_3, self.pv1_3])
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "conflicted")
        self.assertIsNone(result["commonDigest"])

    def test_accepted_may_advance_to_conflicted(self):
        rotated = vpol(2, sites=(JUDGE, JUDGE_B, SITE_A), threshold=2)
        raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_two, [decision_item("c", self.decision_other)],
            old=self.pv1, new=rotated,
        )
        self.assertEqual(parse(raw)["payload"]["status"], "conflicted")
        self.assertEqual(
            self.dvchain(self.root_two, [raw],
                         policies=[self.pv1, rotated])["status"],
            "conflicted")

    def test_accepted_keeps_identical_declaration_under_rotation(self):
        raw = self.dsucc(
            self.root_two, [], old=self.pv1, new=self.pv2_t1)
        payload = parse(raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "accepted")
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["declaration"],
            parse(self.root_two)["payload"]["declaration"])

    def test_two_hop_chain_recomputes_at_each_stage(self):
        first = self.dsucc(
            self.root_one, [decision_item("two", self.decision_b)])
        second = self.dsucc(
            first, [], old=self.pv1, new=self.pv2_t1,
            moment=self.m + 20, effective=self.m + 5)
        result = self.dvchain(
            self.root_one, [first, second],
            policies=[self.pv1, self.pv1, self.pv2_t1], moment=self.m + 30)
        self.assertEqual(result["height"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["policyVersion"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
        self.assertEqual(result["rootDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.root_one).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(result["headDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(second).hexdigest())


class AppendOnlyTest(DecisionAggregateChainFixtures):
    def test_unchanged_policy_requires_non_empty_increment(self):

    def test_rotation_may_reseal_empty_sequence(self):

        self.assertEqual(

class AuthorizationAndMomentTest(DecisionAggregateChainFixtures):
    def test_sealer_must_be_authorized_under_both_policies(self):
        drop = vpol(2, sites=(JUDGE_B,), threshold=1)
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidAggregateChainError):

def _cfca_tally_chain_rows(
    rows: list[dict], prefix_count: int, threshold: int
) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
    """Re-tally the stage rows without rewriting the prefix.

    Identical semantics to :func:`_tally_prune_chain_rows`: a historical
    ``valid`` row of one site/declaration group always wins over a newly
    appended repeat (even one with a smaller id), a second distinct
    declaration from one site contradicts every declaration of that
    site, distinct sites must share the one declaration, and one unique
    conflict-free declaration backed by at least the threshold of
    distinct sites is accepted.  Declarations are compared by their
    complete positional canonical bytes (the common fork edge set, every
    sorted conclusion entry, the term-by-term proof vector and the
    status).
    """
    by_site: dict[str, dict[bytes, list[tuple[bool, dict]]]] = {}
    for position, row in enumerate(rows):
        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] in (
            PA_CONCLUSION_VALID,
            PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE,
            PA_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION,
        ):
            content = _prune_compact(row[PFDA_DECLARATION])
            by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
                content, []
            ).append((position < prefix_count, row))

    contradicted = False
    votes: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    representatives: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for site, groups in by_site.items():
        if len(groups) > 1:
            contradicted = True
            ordered_groups = sorted(
                groups.values(),
                key=lambda members: min(member[1][ID] for member in members),
            )
            for members in ordered_groups:
                members.sort(key=lambda member: member[1][ID])
                members[0][1][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
                members[0][1][ADJ_REASON] = REASON_CONTRADICTION
                for _from_prefix, extra in members[1:]:
                    extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                    extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
        else:
            content, members = next(iter(groups.items()))
            prefix_members = [
                member for member in members if member[0]
            ]
            candidates = prefix_members or members
            winner = min(candidates, key=lambda member: member[1][ID])
            winner[1][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_VALID
            winner[1][ADJ_REASON] = None
            for _from_prefix, member in members:
                if member is winner[1]:
                    continue
                member[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                member[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
            votes[site] = content
            representatives[site] = winner[1]

    contents = set(votes.values())
    if contradicted or len(contents) > 1:
        return PA_STATUS_CONFLICTED, None
    if len(contents) == 1:
        common_declaration = copy.deepcopy(
            min(representatives.values(), key=lambda row: row[ID])[
                PFDA_DECLARATION
            ]
        )
        if len(votes) >= threshold:
            return PA_STATUS_ACCEPTED, common_declaration
        return PA_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT, common_declaration
    return PA_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT, None


def _cfca_recompute(
    prefix_inputs: list[str],
    prefix_rows: list[dict],
    increment: list[dict],
    prune_policy_digest: str,
    fork_site_policy_digest: str,
    fork_threshold: int,
    decision_site_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Recompute the complete stage conclusion from prefix plus increment.

    The prefix statements are the already-verified statements of the
    predecessor; each new decision is authenticated and authorized
    through the existing chain decision aggregate rules under the new
    decision site policy, and the complete statement set is re-tallied.
    """
    increment_rows: list[dict] = []
    increment_digests: list[str] = []
    for item in increment:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(item[CFDA_PACKET]).hexdigest()
        increment_digests.append(digest)
        increment_rows.append(
            _aggregate_cfda_one(
                item,
                prune_policy_digest,
                fork_site_policy_digest,
                fork_threshold,
                decision_site_policy,
                validated_keyring,
                moment,
            )
        )

    full_inputs = list(prefix_inputs) + increment_digests
    working_rows = copy.deepcopy(prefix_rows)
    working_rows.extend(copy.deepcopy(increment_rows))
    status, declaration = _cfca_tally_chain_rows(
        working_rows, len(prefix_rows), decision_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]
    )
    return {
        PFDA_INPUTS: full_inputs,
        PA_ITEMS: _pac_sort_rows(working_rows),
        STATUS: status,
        PFDA_DECLARATION: declaration,
    }

257:## Batch verification and cross-site aggregation of chain fork aggregate decisions
273:`aggregate_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy, decision_site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified signed decisions from distinct decision sites into one signed cross-site aggregate, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `decision` bytes; `prune_policy`, `authorization_policy` and `site_policy` are the shared prune policy, site authorization policy and fork-proof signer site policy the decisions were issued against, and `decision_site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized decision site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the site count); `keyring`/`moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the aggregate signing credentials. Every decision is first re-verified through the exact `verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decision` rules (canonical structure, all three decision policy digest bindings, the term-by-term proof digest bindings and a full re-tally of the bound per-proof rows), then authenticated against the current keyring by its exact payload issuer and key version, then authorized precisely by the payload identity and version against the decision site policy with no fallback: an illegal decision or one with a broken binding is recorded `invalid` with reason `invalid` and carries no identity, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and an authenticated but unauthorized site or key version `unauthorized`; an invalid, unauthenticated or unauthorized decision rejects only that item while later items continue. A valid decision counts as that site's complete declaration: the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions (stably sorted by site then id, each entry carrying its conclusion, proof digest, authenticated fork edges or null, id, reason and site), the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status. For one site, declarations fully identical on every field count once and exact repeats are `duplicate`; any field difference is a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree on that complete declaration: any cross-site declaration difference makes the aggregate `conflicted`, the common declaration is bound null and no majority can outvote the disagreement. One unique declaration backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted`; short of the threshold it stays `insufficient` but keeps that declaration; with no valid vote at all the declaration is null. The aggregate is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `inputs` (each input decision's SHA-256 in the original input order), `issuer`, `items` (the rows stably sorted by issuer then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the decision `digest`, `id`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and the authenticated `declaration` or null), `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest`, `authorizationPolicyDigest`, `sitePolicyDigest`, `decisionSitePolicyDigest`, `declaration` (the one common complete declaration, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1); the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key. A type fault raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); a null value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired aggregate credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision(decision, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such an adjudication entirely offline from just the packet bytes, the expected prune policy, the expected site authorization policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. (The fork-proof site policy is not needed here: it is already digested inside each signed proof the decision rows name.) It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes the two bound policy digests, and re-tallies the bound per-proof rows purely from the signed payload (the stable site/id ordering, the original-order proof digest multiset, the same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, the cross-site complete edge-set agreement, the authorization threshold and the claimed common set), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version usable at the verification moment, so later revocation or expiry rejects it with no fallback. On success it returns a fresh, depth-independent mapping with the fixed keys `common`, `proofDigest` (the SHA-256 of the decision bytes), `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest`, `proofs`, `authorizationPolicyDigest`, `status` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects. A non-bytes decision or a wrong public field type raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; an illegal decision structure or binding raises `InvalidChainDecisionError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from the proof-level `InvalidChainProofError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. All four entry points are purely offline, read and write no file, modify no input, and leave the README commands and the existing replacement-chain, batch-verification and anchor interfaces unchanged.

## Batch verification and cross-site aggregation of chain fork aggregate decisions

The single `verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision` adjudication ruling gets batch re-check and cross-site convergence. The three entry points below reuse the existing adjudication policies, keyring and canonical-encoding rules, read and write no file, modify no input, and add no command-line entry; the README command surface and every existing proof, decision, replacement-chain and anchor interface are unchanged. The per-proof summaries inside each decision are bound term by term to the canonical site/id-sorted rows, so reordering the summaries and re-signing is rejected even though the digest multiset is unchanged.

`verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty, batch-unique list of those adjudication decisions offline and in strict input order. Each item contains exactly a non-empty batch-unique `id` and the non-empty `decision` bytes; the whole batch structure and the shared prune policy, site authorization policy, signer site policy, keyring and moment are validated in full before any decision is parsed, so a type or structure error never yields a partial report (container/element/field faults `TypeError`, a `bool` never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`, with the shared materials keeping their single-decision classification). Each decision is then reported in input order through the exact `verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decision` rules as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one decision's failure never stops a later decision and every failed item keeps a definite non-empty error and a null result. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed key order `error` (null exactly when verified), `id`, `result` (a fresh independent copy of the single-decision result when verified, otherwise null — the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

`aggregate_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy, decision_site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified signed decisions from distinct decision sites into one signed cross-site aggregate, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `decision` bytes; `prune_policy`, `authorization_policy` and `site_policy` are the shared prune policy, site authorization policy and fork-proof signer site policy the decisions were issued against, and `decision_site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized decision site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the site count); `keyring`/`moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the aggregate signing credentials. Every decision is first re-verified through the exact `verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decision` rules (canonical structure, all three decision policy digest bindings, the term-by-term proof digest bindings and a full re-tally of the bound per-proof rows), then authenticated against the current keyring by its exact payload issuer and key version, then authorized precisely by the payload identity and version against the decision site policy with no fallback: an illegal decision or one with a broken binding is recorded `invalid` with reason `invalid` and carries no identity, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and an authenticated but unauthorized site or key version `unauthorized`; an invalid, unauthenticated or unauthorized decision rejects only that item while later items continue. A valid decision counts as that site's complete declaration: the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions (stably sorted by site then id, each entry carrying its conclusion, proof digest, authenticated fork edges or null, id, reason and site), the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status. For one site, declarations fully identical on every field count once and exact repeats are `duplicate`; any field difference is a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree on that complete declaration: any cross-site declaration difference makes the aggregate `conflicted`, the common declaration is bound null and no majority can outvote the disagreement. One unique declaration backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted`; short of the threshold it stays `insufficient` but keeps that declaration; with no valid vote at all the declaration is null. The aggregate is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `inputs` (each input decision's SHA-256 in the original input order), `issuer`, `items` (the rows stably sorted by issuer then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the decision `digest`, `id`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and the authenticated `declaration` or null), `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest`, `authorizationPolicyDigest`, `sitePolicyDigest`, `decisionSitePolicyDigest`, `declaration` (the one common complete declaration, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1); the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key. A type fault raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); a null value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired aggregate credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate(aggregate, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy, decision_site_policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such an aggregate entirely offline from just the aggregate bytes, the four expected policies, the current keyring and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes all four policy digests, and re-tallies the bound per-decision rows purely from the signed payload — the original-order input digest bindings, the issuer/id row ordering, same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, cross-site complete declaration agreement (the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions, the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status together), the threshold outcome and the claimed common declaration — together with a full re-tally of every counted declaration against the signer site policy threshold, and then checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, with no fallback. On success it returns a fresh, depth-independent mapping equal to the authenticated payload plus `aggregateDigest` (the SHA-256 of the aggregate bytes), with the fixed keys `aggregateDigest`, `inputs`, `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest`, `authorizationPolicyDigest`, `sitePolicyDigest`, `decisionSitePolicyDigest`, `declaration`, `status` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects and unauthenticated identities or boundaries never enter a result. A non-bytes aggregate or a wrong public field type raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); a null value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy, threshold or moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal aggregate encoding, key set, digest, ordering, tally or declaration binding raises `InvalidAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from the proof, single-decision and other aggregate errors); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. All three entry points are purely offline, read and write no file, modify no input, and leave the README commands and every existing interface unchanged.

## Supersession chains over cross-site chain fork aggregate decision aggregates

The cross-decision-site chain fork aggregate decision aggregate (`aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions`) gets a replacement chain for supplemental decisions and decision-site-policy rotation. The five entry points below are built on the existing decision aggregate, versioned site policy and keyring rules, read and write no file, modify no input, and add no command-line entry; the README command surface and every existing aggregate, adjudication, proof, chain and anchor interface are unchanged.

`supersede_decision_aggregate(predecessor, increment, prune_policy, authorization_policy, old_policy, new_policy, keyring, moment, effective_at, issuer, version)` issues one signed successor over a chain root (an `aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions` packet) or the previous successor. `increment` is the stage's decision list, each item exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `decision` bytes (an `adjudicate_chain_fork_aggregate_proofs` packet), and may be empty only for a policy rotation. The original `{"batch","sites","threshold"}` prune policy and the site authorization policy are invariant along the whole chain. `old_policy`/`new_policy` are the versioned **decision** site policies and carry exactly `sites`, `threshold` and a positive integer `policyVersion`: unchanged content keeps the version and requires a non-empty increment, any content change increments the version by exactly one, and the first versioned policy over a root carries version 1 and must equal the root's decision site policy. The predecessor's decision digests are the immutable ordered prefix — the two base policies, the root aggregate packet and every prior statement are never deleted, changed or reordered, and a packet or id already in the chain cannot be appended again. The verdict is recomputed in full over the complete history at the effective moment: supplemental decisions may move `insufficient` to `accepted` or `conflicted`, an `accepted` head only keeps the identical common declaration or advances to `conflicted` (it never falls back to insufficient or swaps declarations), and a `conflicted` verdict can never be masked by a later majority. The effective moment never moves backwards. The successor sealer and key version must be authorized under both decision policies and the credential must be usable both at `effective_at` and at the issuance `moment` (the same must hold at verification). The successor is canonical compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds the root digest, predecessor digest, height (the root is height 0), the complete recomputed conclusion (decision digests in original prefix-plus-increment order, the re-tallied rows, the status and common declaration), the invariant prune and site authorization policy digests, the old/new decision policy digests, the policy version, the effective moment, the raw decision increment (bytes as lowercase hex), the issuer and key version and `version` (integer 1), signed with HMAC-SHA256 under the exact issuer/version key. A parameter or public field type fault raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate increment id, an illegal version, a wrong policy count or a backwards moment raises `ValueError`; a malformed root raises `InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`; a malformed successor or broken chain rule raises `InvalidAggregateChainError`; a credential or signature fault raises `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_decision_aggregate_chain(root, successors, prune_policy, authorization_policy, policies, keyring, moment)` verifies one chain hop by hop entirely offline, from just the root bytes, the ordered successor bytes, the two invariant policies, the complete versioned decision site policy history (the root stage policy plus one per successor, so exactly `len(successors) + 1` entries with the first carrying `policyVersion` 1), the current keyring and the verification moment. An empty suffix still verifies the root in full; a non-empty chain additionally recomputes every added decision and the full stage conclusion at each hop, re-checks the root/predecessor/height links, the append-only prefix, the old/new policy digests and single-step version rule, the non-decreasing effective moment, the two invariant policies, the verdict state machine, the dual-policy sealer authorization and the exact-issuer/version HMAC with a credential usable at both the hop's effective moment and the verification moment. On success it returns a fresh mapping with the fixed keys `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height`, `policyVersion`, `status` and `commonDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical common declaration when one is bound, otherwise null). A bad root raises `InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`; a bad successor or chain binding raises `InvalidAggregateChainError`; a credential or signature fault raises `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_decision_aggregate_chains(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch offline and spots cross-chain successor forks. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, its `root` aggregate bytes, its ordered `successors` bytes and its per-stage `policies` history; the whole batch and shared materials are pre-validated in full before any chain is verified, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/field type faults `TypeError`, a `bool` never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, a wrong policy count or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each chain is then run through the exact `verify_decision_aggregate_chain` rules in strict input order and isolation: a root fault reports `invalid-root`, a successor or chain-binding fault `invalid-chain`, a credential or signature fault `unauthenticated` (each with a null result and a non-empty error), and a passing chain `verified`. Verified chains are grouped by `rootDigest` and only successor trajectories under the same root are compared: the same predecessor digest pointing at two distinct successor digests is a fork, while a plain prefix extension (one chain growing longer along the same packets) is not. Every verified chain crossing a forking edge is reclassified `conflicted` with its verified result kept and its error fixed to `forked-decision-aggregate-chain`; invalid or unauthenticated chains are never reclassified. The result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys `forks`, `items` and `version` (integer 1); `forks` is stably sorted by `rootDigest` then `predecessorDigest`, each entry carrying exactly `rootDigest`, `predecessorDigest`, `successors` (the forking successor digests, ascending) and `ids` (the ascending ids of the chains crossing the edge), and each item report keeps input order with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result`, `status`; failure results are null and fork summaries and crossing ids are stably ascending.

`seal_decision_aggregate_head(items, target, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` seals a stable anchor only for the `target` chain within the batch that is `verified` (not conflicted by a fork in this batch, invalid or unauthenticated) and whose head is `accepted`; another chain's failure never stops the target's anchor, though a fork it shares still reclassifies the target. The anchor is canonical compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly the target's root digest, head digest, height, the head decision policy digest, the head policy version and the sealing moment, signed with HMAC-SHA256 under the exact issuer/version key usable at `moment`. Sealing a batch that is not fully pre-validated, an unknown or empty target, a non-accepted or forked target, an illegal version or a wrong policy count raises `ValueError`; a malformed target root raises `InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`; a bad successor or chain binding raises `InvalidAggregateChainError`; a signing credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. `verify_decision_aggregate_head(anchor, items, target, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring, moment)` re-verifies the anchor structurally and its HMAC against the current exact-issuer/version key usable at the verification moment, requires the sealing moment not to be later than the verification moment, re-runs the whole batch and confirms the target still verifies with no fork and an accepted head, and that the bound root digest, head digest, height, head policy digest, policy version and sealing moment still match; it returns a fresh mapping with the fixed keys `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height`, `policyDigest`, `policyVersion` and `anchorDigest` (the SHA-256 of the anchor bytes). A bad anchor raises `InvalidAggregateAnchorError`; a malformed root raises `InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError`; a bad successor or chain binding raises `InvalidAggregateChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. `InvalidAggregateChainError` and `InvalidAggregateAnchorError` both subclass `ValueError`, and `AuthenticationError` keeps its existing classification. Every entry is purely offline, reads and writes no file, modifies no input, and leaves the README commands and every existing interface unchanged.
